questions.problem: Rewrite the statement $¬((A∧B)∧(A∨¬B))$ using De Morgan's laws.
questions.worked_solution:
De Morgan's laws state that

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(A∧B)≡¬A∨¬B, \\ ¬(A∨B)≡¬A∧¬B.\end{aligned}
$$

So, we can simplify the given statement as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}¬((A∧B)∧(A∨¬B)) & ≡¬(A∧B)∨¬(A∨¬B) \\  & ≡(¬A∨¬B)∨(¬A∧¬(¬B)) \\  & ≡(¬A∨¬B)∨(¬A∧B)\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$\,$ $n$ is not divisible by $3$ and $n$ is not divisible by $5.$

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
questions.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law posits that the negation of a conjunction of two statements is equivalent to the disjunction of the negated individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows.

$$
¬(A∧B)=¬A∨¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,\,¬(n\text{ is not divisible by }3\text{ and } & n\text{ is not divisible by }5) \\  & ≡¬((n\text{ is not divisible by }3)∧(n\text{ is not divisible by }5)) \\  & ≡¬(n\text{ is not divisible by }3)∨¬(n\text{ is not divisible by }5) \\  & ≡(n\text{ is divisible by }3)∨(n\text{ is divisible by }5) \\  & ≡n\text{ is divisible by }3\text{ or }n\text{ is divisible by }5.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
$\,$ $2$ is not prime or $2\notin Q.$

What is the negation of the compound statement above?
questions.worked_solution:
De Morgan's law for disjunctions states that the negation of a disjunction of two statements is equivalent to the conjunction of the negations of the individual statements. It can be stated symbolically as follows:

$$
¬(A∨B)=¬A∧¬B
$$

So, the negation of our statement is

$$
\begin{aligned}¬(2\text{ is not prime}\text{ or }2\notin Q) & ≡¬((2\text{ is not prime})∨(2\notin Q)) \\  & ≡¬(2\text{ is not prime})∧¬(2\notin Q) \\  & ≡(2\text{ is prime})∧(2\in Q) \\  & ≡2\text{ is prime}\text{ and }2\in Q.\end{aligned}
$$
